honestStatement: No Android App Bundle signed by the production upload key exists as of this record. An AAB file existing would not by itself make it ready; the gates below are what must be satisfied, and the code paths that satisfy them are now in the repository but have never executed end to end.
whyNotProduced: Before this pass, no lane that actually runs ever built a bundle: tools/android-ci-release.sh invoked only assembleRelease, and bundleRelease existed solely in .github/workflows/knoux-live-release.yml, which fires on a tag push or manual dispatch and has never published.
The lane that can build a bundle also silently fell back to a disposable CI keystore whenever the production secrets were absent, and uploaded the result to a public GitHub Release anyway.

The production secrets are incomplete. As of this record the android-production environment holds 2 of the 5 expected values, both non-secret and uploaded during this session: KNOUX_ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS and KNOUX_ANDROID_CERT_SHA256. The three that carry secret material — KNOUX_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64, KNOUX_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD and KNOUX_ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD — are UNVERIFIED AS UPLOADED and are owner-only. Repository-level secrets remain 0. Because the gate requires all five, every publishable run still fails closed.
The Google Play App Signing option (Google-managed app signing key versus owner-managed) has not been chosen by the owner, and enrollment is irreversible.

fixedInThisPass.acceptanceLaneNowBuildsBundle: tools/android-ci-release.sh now runs './gradlew assembleRelease bundleRelease' so a bundle is produced and verified on every release acceptance run
fixedInThisPass.sharedIdentityGate: tools/verify-production-signing-identity.cjs is called by both lanes before any build work
fixedInThisPass.crossArtifactIdentityCheck: APK and AAB signer certificate SHA-256 digests are compared and the build fails if they differ
fixedInThisPass.productionPinRecheckedOnArtifacts: in production mode both the APK and the AAB certificate must equal KNOUX_ANDROID_CERT_SHA256 after signing, not merely before
fixedInThisPass.publishRefusesCiIdentity: knoux-live-release.yml publish job requires android.signing == production and a recorded certificate fingerprint
fixedInThisPass.noPlaintextPasswords: apksigner uses env:, jarsigner and keytool use -storepass:env
fixedInThisPass.explicitStoreType: PKCS12 is passed explicitly; previously the .p12 was written to a file named .jks with no store type, risking a silent load failure into the CI branch
fixedInThisPass.signingStepWorkingDirectory: A pre-existing structural defect was found while reviewing this as an execution path rather than as unit tests: the signing step of knoux-live-release.yml had no working-directory, so it ran at the workspace root where app/build/outputs/... does not exist, and wrote ../release-android outside the checkout while every later step reads release-android/ at the root. That job could never have completed. It is now fixed, and it is still unexecuted.

identityExpected.uploadCertificateSubject: CN=KNOUX X Android Production, OU=Engineering, O=KNOUX X, L=Abu Dhabi, ST=Abu Dhabi, C=AE
identityExpected.playAppSigningDistributionCertificate: UNKNOWN - assigned by Google at enrollment; must be recorded separately and never conflated with the upload fingerprint
identityExpected.identityVerifiedBy: keytool -printcert on the exported public certificate PEM, cross-checked against the owner's PUBLIC-CERTIFICATE-INFO.txt; the keystore itself was not opened and no password was requested or entered

releaseApkEvidenceForContext.note: This is the acceptance-lane APK, NOT a production artifact. It is recorded because it is the only real installed build that exists.
releaseApkEvidenceForContext.certificateSubject: CN=Knoux X CI Release Verification, OU=CI, O=Knoux X, L=Abu Dhabi, ST=Abu Dhabi, C=AE
releaseApkEvidenceForContext.webContentsDebuggingNote: true is required for the acceptance lane to drive an installed WebView and is asserted to be false in production mode; this artifact must never reach any release channel
releaseApkEvidenceForContext.independentlyVerifiedWith: tools/verify-apk-signing-block.cjs, which parses the APK Signing Block and prints the certificate through keytool without needing an Android SDK

A_source.detail: clean approved commit, branch protection satisfied, no secrets in git, version identity validated by tools/knoux-release-version.cjs

B_build.detail: deterministic lockfile enforced; Capacitor bridge generated per build; assembleRelease and bundleRelease now both run; production configuration asserted

C_cryptographic_verification.blockedBy: owner must upload the five secrets to the android-production environment and resolve its branch policy
C_cryptographic_verification.detail: the gate exists and passes 29 behavioural tests against throwaway keystores driven by real keytool; it has NEVER run against the owner's production identity, so no signing fix in this record may be described as verified at production level

D_runtime.detail: emulator smoke passes for the acceptance APK; bundletool has never been run because it is not installed on this workstation and no AAB exists; no physical device has run any build

E_policy.detail: target API 36 satisfied; 16 KB satisfied by evidence (zero native libraries); permissions matrix written and the unused CAMERA removed; privacy policy drafted in both languages but not hosted; foreground-service declarations and the demonstration video do not exist

F_play_console.blockedBy: owner: confirm the developer account exists and its type, create the app entry, choose and enroll a Play App Signing option

G_production_approval.detail: explicit owner approval against an exact AAB hash is required; approval of a branch is not approval of an artifact

commandsThatWillProduceTheRealRecord: gh workflow run knoux-live-release.yml --ref main -f mode=draft   # builds and verifies an AAB without publishing
bundletool install-apks --apks=...   # on a real device, then run the journeys in 04-android-functional-matrix.md
claimBoundary: Code-level correctness is tested. Production-level behaviour is not, because no run has used the approved production identity. Both statements are kept apart deliberately.
